value.body: Social workers support people and communities facing problems such as poverty, abuse, disability, illness or displacement. They work in NGOs, hospitals, schools, CSR foundations and government schemes, and the day can involve field visits, counselling, case records, linking people to schemes and running community programmes.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BA (Sociology or related), BSW, then usually an MSW

items.label: Common settings
items.value: NGOs, hospitals, schools, CSR foundations, government programmes

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A BA can lead to field or community-worker roles in NGOs and programmes. A Master of Social Work (MSW) is the usual qualification for case-work, medical, psychiatric and many CSR roles; fellowships run by development organisations are another entry point.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Knowledge of government welfare schemes and laws
Working with local government and other agencies

value.title: At a glance
items: Much of the work is field-based and emotionally demanding.
Common next steps: programme coordinator, project manager, or specialised counselling roles.
Many NGO roles are tied to project funding.
